description.narrative: OSWD har genom sitt Forskarutbildningsprogram erbjudit stipendier för forskarutbildning inom basvetenskaperna till unga kvinnor sedan 1998. Programmet är öppet för kvinnor under 40 år, från länder i Afrika söder om Sahara och låginkomstländer. Kvalifikationskrav är en masterexamen eller en kandidatexamen med extraordinärt goda betyg ino

The OWSD has through its Postgraduate Training Fellowships offered scholarship for research training in the natural sciences to young women since 1998. The programme is open for women under forty years of age from Sub-Saharan Africa and other low-income countries. The entry requirement is either an MSc degree or an outstanding BSc honours degree in a natural scientific field.
To increase women's participation, particularly young female scientists, leadership and influence in science and technology in developing countries.

OWSD's flagship programme for the last 20 years has been the PhD fellowships programme. 254 women have received fellowships in the period (2012- April 2017) from countries facing huge challenges in obtaining funding and undertaking scientific research. 96 of these women have graduated between January 2012 and April 2017 (out of a total of 214 graduates since January 1998). Many have returned to their home countries after receiving their PhDs and are mentors and supervisors for young women and men in their field. There are currently 199 fellowship holders on site in countries throughout the developing world. OWSD provides a travel fund of up to USD5,000 per fellowship, ensuring that awardees have an opportunity to extend their networks by attending conferences and workshops. From 2013 when the fund was first disbursed until April 2017, 151 fellows have taken up this opportunity, attending 215 conferences.
Examples of a positive result for GenderInSITE: The Latin America Carribean focal point has been particularly successful in its actions with the OAS, the Organization of American States, a multilateral regional organization that includes all countries in the American continent. In 2014 the focal point participated in the 4th Meeting of the Ministers of Science and was central in providing the text for a paragraph on gender, science and development signed by all Ministers present. This led to an annual follow up through the COMCYT, the Inter-American Committee on Science and Technology of the OAS, where many member countries requested more specific guidance on how to structure relevant gender policies in science, with several online meetings being held.
